source.title: Phases of learning dynamics in artificial neural networks: with or without mislabeled data

record.tranche_reason: Tests how fitting mislabeled training samples relates to test error, using mixed-label datasets and learning-dynamics measurements rather than the original fixed-random-label comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fitting random labels, but does not count those cited results as its own. Its own mixed-label experiments report training and test error dynamics and a label-cleaning result.
record.test_reason: The mixed-label experiments test V1's memorization-capacity component: an ordinarily trained network fits fixed random labels alongside correct labels. They do not establish V1's clean-label versus fully random-label generalization comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors distinguish four noisy-label learning phases, associate them with gradient alignment and strength, and demonstrate improved generalization through phase-II loss-based cleaning. They also report no significant difference between cleaning and early stopping in their experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD on datasets with varying fractions of randomly mislabeled samples and tracks test error and learning dynamics; does not reproduce the fixed random-label comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The test-error trajectory and final test error vary with the mislabeled fraction ρ; the minimum test error rises sharply past a threshold and approaches the final error when ρ > 0.85.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error stays low initially and rises while the network fits corrupted labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under mixed-label training, learning correct labels precedes memorizing corrupted labels, with later memorization worsening clean-test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Phase-II loss-based cleaning improves noisy-MNIST test accuracy, recovering over half the gap to training on only correctly labeled examples through noise levels of 80%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing high-loss examples during maximal loss-distribution separation improves generalization under label corruption.

record.problems: The authors say the study uses realistic but simple datasets and pays less attention to absolute performance. Test-error curves are mainly presented in figures, and numerical values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fully random-label training with the same architecture and recipe; near-perfect fit on fully random labels; held-out natural-label accuracy far above chance versus chance-level held-out accuracy under fully random labeling; absence of explicit regularization is not documented.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparative held-out performance of convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of locality.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps. Gradient-noise spectra do not measure this relationship.
Removal by inclusion-based memorization scores, retraining, and comparison with equal-sized random removals.

missing.what: The authors also report similar four-phase mixed-label learning results on CIFAR-10, including the phase in which all training labels are fitted. Architecture, numerical errors, and experimental details are not supplied.
missing.locator: Section 4, paragraph introducing the four phases

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope verdict confuses untested components with contrary evidence. Increased test error after corrupt-label fitting is compatible with V1. No verdict is warranted on the full coexistence comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the exact V1 setup of fitting a fully random-label dataset and a clean natural-label dataset with the same architecture and recipe, or report held-out accuracy at chance on fully random labels.
The study removes samples with high loss as a label-cleaning procedure; it does not identify examples by how much their inclusion raises the chance of predicting their own label.

rows.subject: fully connected network with two hidden layer (50 hidden units per layer)
rows.size_stated: two hidden layers, 50 hidden units per layer; subset of MNIST data with 400 samples per digit
rows.operation_detail: Trained with randomly mislabeled samples at different fractions ρ; tracked test error through four learning phases.

conditions.value: different values of ρ; exact values not stated in the text

rows.measure: Test error over training; decreases during phase I, stays roughly the same during phase II, rises during phase III, and reaches a high plateau during phase IV. Across noise levels, final test error increases with ρ; minimum test error rises sharply past a threshold and approaches final test error when ρ > 0.85.
rows.note: The text describes the trajectory and dependence on ρ, but does not give numerical test-error values. This is a mixed-label experiment, not the fully random-label comparison in V1.
rows.check: The noisy-training test-error trajectory measures interference from label corruption. Its later rise does not limit V1, which does not predict preserved clean-label accuracy after fitting corrupted labels. Neither a matched clean-label comparison nor chance-level performance with fully random labels is established.

rows.subject: fully connected network with two hidden layer (50 hidden units per layer)
rows.size_stated: two hidden layers, 50 hidden units per layer; subset of MNIST data with 400 samples per digit
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training errors on correctly labeled and randomly mislabeled samples while training on their mixture.

conditions.value: different values of ρ; exact values not stated in the text

rows.measure: Training errors for both correctly and incorrectly labeled data decrease to zero during phase III; the network finds a solution satisfying both sets of training samples.
rows.value: 0 training error during phase III, as stated in text
rows.note: Training fit is reported for a mixture of correct and random labels; this does not establish the V1 all-random-label condition.
rows.check: Valid evidence for the memorization-capacity component only: Section 4 states that errors on both correct and random training labels decrease to zero. This is a mixed-label dataset, not a demonstrated fully random-label fit.

rows.subject: fully connected network with two hidden layer (50 hidden units per layer)
rows.size_stated: two hidden layers, 50 hidden units per layer; MNIST dataset
rows.operation_detail: Removed samples above a loss threshold at a cleaning time chosen when the fitted loss-mean separation was maximal, then continued training on the cleaned dataset.

conditions.value: 50% in Fig. 6(A)–(D); varying ρ in Fig. 6(E)

rows.measure: Test accuracy with cleaning versus without cleaning; the authors report significant improvement in generalization for noise levels up to ρ = 80%.
rows.value: test accuracy with cleaning, ac; figure only
rows.note: This is the paper's loss-based label-cleaning procedure, not removal based on the influence criterion in V8.
rows.check: The reported cleaning improvement is valid but measures no listed version, so observed is inappropriate relative to these claims. Figure 6 uses the same MNIST subset and network as Figure 3. Selection uses loss, not V8's inclusion-based memorization criterion, and there is no matched random-removal control.

relationships.condition: Memorization-capacity component only; two-hidden-layer MNIST network trained on mixed correct and fixed random labels
relationships.reason: R2 reports zero training error on both label groups, supporting capacity to memorize random labels; the broader clean-versus-random generalization comparison remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: The reported zero training error on both label groups remains unverified, and the paired clean-versus-random held-out comparison was untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Training error reaches zero on both correctly and randomly labeled samples, but test error rises during later fitting phases; the study does not test fully random labels or compare the exact clean-versus-random setup (R1, R2).
